items.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued November 14 at 1:14PM CST until November 16 at 12:00PM CST by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
items.description:
* WHAT...High risk of rip currents. Minor coastal flooding
possible around high tide times late Sunday into Monday
morning.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda
Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Strong winds and elevated seas
will drive wave runup further up the beach than is typically
normal. There is a risk of minor coastal flooding along the
low lying areas from the Bolivar Peninsula to Surfside around
high tide times late Sunday into Monday.
items.instruction: Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 14 at 1:12PM CST until November 15 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Small Craft Advisory, southeast winds 20 to 25
kt with gusts up to 30 kt and Gulf seas 6 to 9 ft expected. For
the Gale Watch, northeast winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 40
kt and Gulf seas 8 to 13 ft possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Gulf of America.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 6 PM CST Sunday.
For the Gale Watch, from Sunday evening through Monday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds can cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should consider altering plans to avoid possible
hazardous conditions.  Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter
course, and/or secure the vessel for severe wind and seas.
